content.text: The verifier confirms compliance; I'll repair the finding so the 90-day figure isn't mistaken for a non-renewal notice window.

input.quote: For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
input.rationale: Compliant at the preferred position. §10 (p0065) provides a "renewable one-year term" for maintenance, and the Agreement contains no "automatically renew" or "unless either party gives notice ... days prior" language anywhere (searches for renewal, term-extension and fee-increase wording return only p0065). Renewal therefore requires the parties' agreement in 12-month periods, which is the preferred outcome, and there is no non-renewal notice window to compute and no multi-year auto-renewal, so neither the fallback (≤60 days) nor the walk-away (>90 days / multi-year) thresholds are engaged. §17(a) (p0117) reinforces this: the licence continues perpetually while fees are paid under the Fee Schedule. The only 90-day figure in the document is §17(b), Sparkling's own termination-for-convenience notice right; that is a customer-side exit right benefiting us, not a non-renewal notice window imposed on us, so it is not a RENEWAL deviation and is not flagged. Noted as a sub-element only: there is no cap on maintenance fee uplift on renewal (§11 simply cross-refers to the Fee Schedule), whereas the preferred position caps increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%; per the playbook a missing price-uplift cap is a rationale note rather than a deviation, and we can pursue it commercially if the Fee Schedule permits unilateral increases.
